newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB ships grain to US Gulf ports in past six weeks.
newsitem.headline: CWB ships grain to US Gulf ports in past six weeks.

text.p: Canadian Wheat Board already shipped a small amount of grain in the past six weeks through U.S. Gulf ports because of a backlog at Canada's Pacific ports, a CWB spokeswoman said.

"We shipped 3,000 tonnes (of durum wheat) last summer, so it would be similar amounts. We've done four or five shipments in the last month and a half. It's certainly not ship cargoes, like 25,000 tonnes. It's incremental volumes at these higher prices we're seeing now and not greater," CWB spokeswoman Deanna Allen said.
Forty ships waited to load Monday at Canada Pacific ports.
One ship was berthed for 46 days, the CWB said.
CWB said it faces C$15 million in demurrage fines because of the delays since early January and passed on new sales for February, March shipment. April sales were at risk.

CWB shipped one train load of grain through the U.S. to Portland, Oregon, during the March 1995 port strike in Vancouver. The agency also shipped grain to Latin America last summer through U.S. Gulf ports.
Rail costs through the U.S. range between C$7 to C$30 a tonne more than in Canada, the CWB has said.
Grain shipped since January was trucked to U.S. elevators.
"The grain is trucked down and it's either direct rail or sent by way of the Mississippi," Allen said.
